articleTitle: Smart IoT platform for Big Data analysis in predictive maintenance
abstract: A smart IoT platform for big data analysis in predictive maintenance can help achieve goals of predictive maintenance by collection, processing, and analysis of data from various sensors. This platform can use machine learning algorithms and other advanced techniques to identify patterns and trends that can be used to predict when equipment is likely to fail, allowing maintenance teams to take proactive action to prevent those failures from occurring.

articleTitle: Accuracy testing of a mobile robot position identifying in 3D space
abstract: The paper presents three object localisation methods in 3D space using a laser scanner sensor as a measured reference signal. The authors used the Velodyne LIDAR sensor and Matlab software to realise the described algorithms for position calculation. The article presents the accuracy of localisation depending on the applied spatial position identification method. The accuracy was separately determined for translation, rotation, and simultaneous translation with rotation. The translation accuracy was dependent on the shift axis. The limitations of the considered methods were also presented, along with a proposal to improve accuracy. The presented algorithms can be successfully applied to find the position of autonomous mobile robots in confined spaces such as public buildings, offices, and technological halls.

articleTitle: A Cluster enabled Blockchain-based Data management for IoT systems
abstract: Internet of Things a flourishing societal luxury has seen massive evolutionary trends that have revolutionized the need for secure and competent data management schemes. Data Privacy, trust, and security in the IoT environment are essential matters that need confronting, especially when gathered data is prone to malicious attacks or activities. Moreso, latency requirements that rise exponentially with each added device necessitate effective management in order to meet expected Quality of Service standards. Blockchain-based IoT, a paradigm that decentralizes IoT’s topology has earned growing popularity over the years owing to its versatility, however, most works on Blockchain-based IoT focus on perspectives such as digital currencies, consensus algorithms, and smart contracts, with very few delving into Blockchain’s role in data management. Therefore, to solve the above-mentioned problems, this study proposes a three-tiered scheme, incorporating aspects of clustering, Edge-Computing, and Blockchain, that focuses on data management mechanism of the Blockchain architecture and data structure. The three-tiered framework aims to provide a decentralised, secure resource optimization and data management mechanism for IoT systems that includes permissioned authentication protocol for all nodes of contention, smart contract generation between permissioned nodes, immutable block transactions and node deployment, not limited or bound by a singular node. The first phase of the methodology presenting the framework paves way for the second phase of the methodology which evaluates and analyses the proposed scheme, thus illustrating how clustering, blockchain and edge computing bring about an efficient paradigm for tamper-resistant data management with improved latency and high-level credibility and security suitable for IoT systems.

articleTitle: Design of nonlinear MPC techniques for Indoor Air Quality control
abstract: Indoor Air Quality control represents a crucial aspect in Home & Building Automation together with thermal comfort, lighting comfort and energy saving. The present paper proposes different MPC tuning strategies for Indoor Air Quality control in an office through natural ventilation, focusing on the impact of the prediction horizon. A reliable and flexible simulation framework is designed in order to straightly test and simulate the developed control strategies. Nonlinear Model Predictive Control is designed as control strategy. Carbon dioxide is selected as controlled variable that is characterized by an upper constraint. The manipulated variable is represented by the opening width of the office windows. Occupancy and wind speed are considered in the control systems’ formulation. The proposed controllers are tested and compared through simulation.

articleTitle: Fast Joint Image Compression-Encryption Algorithm used for 3D Reconstruction
abstract: This paper presents a JPEG-improved algorithm for compression and encryption of 2D structured light images applied in 3D reconstruction. The proposed method incorporates compression and encryption simultaneously to achieve a high compression ratio while adding security without affecting 3D reconstruction. The 2D structured light image is divided into 8×8 blocks, then DCT is applied for each block followed by an optimized JPEG-based quantization matrix. The resulting blocks are merged in a single matrix, and the DC coefficients in each column are subjected to first-order difference to reduce the Min-Max span for fast decoding. The decompression is accomplished reversely, and a fast sequential search method is proposed based on a conventional searching approach. The results showed achieving up to a 98% compression ratio of 2D structured light images while maintaining successful and accurate 3D reconstruction. Moreover, the execution time decreased significantly by (61%-80%).

articleTitle: Design, Modeling and Control of an Over-actuated Hexacopter Tilt-Rotor
abstract: This work presents the modeling, control, and simulation of a new Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) prototype, of an over-actuated Hexacopter Tilt-Rotor (HTR) type. Regarding its topology, 2 of the 6 actuators are independently tilted by servomotors. This possibility gives the HTR higher maneuver-ability and reliability. In this combination, every propulsion motor and servomotor has its Real Control Action (RCA) processed simply and with low computational cost procedures since the control allocation technique can be embedded even in traditional control boards. Furthermore, this control allocation will increase the vehicle’s yaw capability and steering control. The control structure used is a cascaded loop of Proportional (P)-Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers with the Successive Loop Closure (SLC), in all 5 manipulated Degrees of Freedom (DoF). The results conclude that flights presented reasonable stability and maneuverability.

articleTitle: Sizing pipes without iterative calculus: Solutions for head loss, flow discharge and diameter
abstract: Solutions for the three main problems in sizing of pipes that usually occurs in engineering practice are given: 1. head loss Δh, 2. flow discharge Q, and 3. diameter D. In turbulent flow, iterative calculus can be easily avoided only in solution of flow discharge Q, while head loss Δh and diameter D can be only calculated through various approximate but accurate non-iterative procedures. This article describes relevant solutions for the observed problems and compares them in numerical examples.

articleTitle: Heat Transport Modeling And Model-Based Temperature Control Of A Residential Building, A Case Study
abstract: The paper proposes a case study on modeling, model validation, model-based temperature control of a building to demonstrate the effectiveness of a modern control technique versus a classical control used in a residential building. Energy efficiency is a key topic today, thus it is important to study the methods of temperature control in buildings to achieve the desired control with minimum energy usage. The paper presents the heat transport modeling using the R-C model technique, the model validation (parameter tuning) based on long-term measurements, classical control and model-based predictive (MPC) distributed temperature control in the rooms of the building and the comparison of the energy consumption for each case. Moreover, there are two MPC algorithms discussed, with and without external temperature forecast as disturbance variable. The simulation results and real-time measurements are presented.

articleTitle: A Technical Investigation towards a Cloud-Based Signature Solution
abstract: This paper proposes a technical investigation towards a solution for a cloud-based signature architecture. Based on the main concepts and ideas available today in this field, our proposed approach integrates seven components to cover all the determined functional and non-functional requirements of such a system.

articleTitle: Design of a Model Predictive Controller for a Linear Hydraulic Motor
abstract: This paper presents the application of a MPC controller for a linear hydraulic motor. The mathematical model of a linear hydraulic motor was designed using a proportional servo valve. The analysis of the choice of the controller’s adjustable parameters and the achieved control performance will be presented. This paper aims to find out which set of adjustable parameters of the predictive controller is optimal for the given type of system, as the highest quality of a control process achieved.

articleTitle: Position Control of Active Arms of Da Vinci Robotic Surgical System
abstract: The present work presents a way of controlling the position of the active arms of a Da Vinci-type surgical robot. The automatic control for positioning the active arms in the desired positions is considered the existence of a camera placed on the slave system of the Da Vinci robot to provide us with information from these positions. In analysing the position error of the robot's active arm, we will compare the arm's current position versus the target position. The method will be applied to each robotic arm separately. By this, we want to show that the presence of medical staff to handle these arms manually is no longer necessary. Once these positions are reached, the surgeon can begin the surgical intervention.

articleTitle: A PSO Tuning ANN for Extracting the MPP from a DC Microgrid System under Changing Irradiance
abstract: The application of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) tuning for Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) is an effective method for maximizing power output from photovoltaic (PV) panels in a DC microgrid system under changing irradiance conditions. This technique can be used to optimize the performance of a PV system, particularly in locations with variable weather conditions. This study proposes a new approach of implementing ANN that is tuned using practical swarm optimization technique. The ANN is trained using data generated by MATLAB Software on the weather conditions and the power output of the PV system and the PSO algorithm is then used to tune the parameters of the ANN model. The optimized ANN model can then be under severe proposed changes in irradiance and to adjust the power converter to achieve the maximum power output. The DC microgrid system used in this study is composed of multiple PV panels and battery along with a super capacitor for a storage system to feed a resistive load. The results of this study illustrate that the PSO tuning of ANNs is an effective method for maximizing power output from PV panels in a DC microgrid system under changing irradiance conditions reaching a precision of 99.7% from the PV panels and response time of 0.11s.

articleTitle: The Use of Anti-Windup Techniques in Didactic Level Systems: An Interesting Application
abstract: Living in the age of technology and industrial evolution, automation applications are increasingly used and more necessary, either to improve the quality of a product or even cheapen some processes. Methods of Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) (such as its variants) tuning controllers have been much discussed due to their effectiveness. Taking this into consideration, the proposed work aims to improve the level controller in PD3 SMAR didactic plant. This level system always presents actuator saturation which leads to overshooting of the controlled response, decreasing the quality, consequently. To avoid this problem, the Back-Calculation Anti-Windup technique was considered. The Proportional and Integral (PI) control was performed directly at the plant via MATLAB software. The results showed that the use of Anti-Windup techniques became useful and reliable in systems where the actuator saturation was strongly present.

articleTitle: Self-Scanning System and Evaluation of Dynamic Electrical Performance of Electric Vehicles Using Different Control Systems
abstract: The main energy target of an electric vehicle (EV) is reducing the consumption by optimally using battery energy between two successive charges and travelling the greatest possible distance in any dynamic conditions. An EV’s power converter must at all times use the optimal amount of energy supplied from the batteries to fulfil this purpose. It is necessary to change the control strategy of the motors while driving the electric vehicle depending on the operating mode. The definition and selection of optimal intelligent control techniques are determined by the measurement and the determination of operating boundary conditions according to the working modes of the electric vehicle. The EV can operate with one or two motors - all wheel drive (AWD) - depending on the operating mode. The main regimes considered are acceleration, braking, skidding regime by varying the adhesion torque as well as changing the traction system by coupling two motors on the two axles - front and rear – (AWD). This paper presents an innovative technique for detecting the optimal control method of an EV driven by a three-phase inverter depending on the operating regimes of the vehicle. The analysed control strategies were scalar control (U/f), direct torque control (DTC) and field-oriented control (FOC). A comparative study between the different control strategies by measuring and analysing the motor torque and the harmonic spectrum of the stator current is carried out in the paper. The comparative study focuses on determining the optimal values of the global energy parameters of a battery-powered EV using different control algorithms. The result of this comparison determines the strengths and weaknesses of the different techniques by evaluating the energy performance of the EV under imposed dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Implementation of learning algorithm for rescue system with uncertainty
abstract: Planning the arrival of an emergency vehicle in times of increasing traffic density is influenced by many factors that can be classified as random events. Changing conditions in road traffic during the day cause uncertainty in the time required for the arrival of an emergency vehicle. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a suitable learning algorithm that would help the dispatcher to determine from which emergency service station the first aid should be provided. When calculating the arrival time, the degree of uncertainty determined by the current traffic situation on the route from the emergency service station to the place of intervention will be used. We will start from the Lamarckian design of learning with the help of rewards and after the appropriate generalization we will incorporate this approach into hyperheuristics.

articleTitle: Semi-active vehicle suspension with SMC controller
abstract: This article presents the synthesis of a sliding control for a semi-active vibration reduction system. The subject of the research is synthesizing a sliding regulator for a suspension strut of a vehicle. In this case, the active element is the controlled damper. The authors determined the characteristics of vibration transmission, allowing for the evaluation of the quality of the vibration reduction system depending on the choice of the sliding surface. Sliding control methods are robust. For this reason, the impact of the uncertainty of the parameters of the suspension model and the semi-active element on the control quality was limited. The road roughness (irregularities) included in the object model and the disturbances changes authors consider as the model parameter uncertainty. Overall, a semi-active suspension system and a sliding mode controller can provide improved ride comfort, handling, and stability for a vehicle compared to the passive suspension system.

articleTitle: The Lotka-Volterra Model for Competition Controlled by a Sliding Mode Approach
abstract: This paper deals with a variation of the Lotka-Volterra model and its control using Sliding Mode Control (SMC). The Lotka-Volterra model consists of two nonlinear equations of the equilibrium region, where they are calculated and their local stability analysis and a design of a controller are conducted using the Lyapunov approach. After that, this paper presents the system’s control in asymptotical stable and unstable regions. The proposed control strategy is an SMC strategy, which in fact is robust for parameter variations and disturbances. Often, the Lotka-Volterra model parameters are difficult to be identified or they are identified with large uncertainties because they can change over time. Simulation results are shown to demonstrate the proposed control strategy performance.

articleTitle: Process of finding human knee in image based on multiple weighted thresholding and histograms of gradients
abstract: Osteoarthritis is the most common joint disease, affecting about 12% of the population. It mainly affects the weight-bearing hip and knee joints but is also commonly found in other locations (spine, shoulder, elbow, and fingers). In Osteoarthritis, the articular cartilage is gradually destroyed, and its mechanical properties are altered, typically manifested externally by pain, frequent inflammation, and swelling.As part of the clinical needs of physicians, regular monitoring and recording of knee conditions are advisable during the follow-up and treatment of the disease. This paper proposes a process to obtain an image of the knee using a camera mounted on a sliding stand. To ensure the repeatability of the image acquisition, a software process is presented that allows finding the knee in the image. The found knee can be used in the unattended device to move the camera to an optimal position corresponding to the centre of the patient’s knee.

articleTitle: Applications for Automatic C Code Assessment
abstract: Software systems that allow for automatic code assessment are highly demanded in educational context to automate the evaluation of program codes implemented by students. These tools can be used to improve the engagement of computer science students in programming courses by providing quick feedback on their work. Although there exists a great number of such tools, most of them are developed for a specific course or lack advanced features that are required for certain pedagogical goals, such as Git integration. In this paper we present two applications for automatic C code assessment. At first, we have developed a web-based automatic code assessment system with Hungarian GUI for checking C program codes. Next, we have employed GitHub and GitHub Classroom for the same purpose with the same set of programming assignments to compare the benefits and impact of the two systems on our novice computer science students.

articleTitle: Examination of the possibility of adapting the PI algorithm
abstract: The article examines what kind of PI control problems can occur when replacing a PLC (Programmable Logic Controller). In industry, it happens that the PLC breaks down or is out of date, so it has to be replaced. The research shows how to create the algorithmization of the PI (Proportional Integral) algorithm written in the FBD (Function Block Diagram) programming language of the individual manufacturer. After tuning the algorithm, we can transfer the tuned parameters and the algorithm to the other PLC. It examines whether programs written in different PLCs can be specifically adapted by PI control into another controller. It reveals what functional and quality differences are experienced during the examination.

articleTitle: Two Objective Emergency Medical Service System Design with Limited Price of Fairness
abstract: Designer of any public service system faces at least two contradictory objectives. The first of them is so-called system criterion, which minimizes average disutility perceived by the system users. The secondary criterion often denoted as criterion of fairness consists of minimizing system disutility perceived by the users. The two objectives stay in a conflict, which manifests itself in the fact that any improvement of one of the criteria is paid by worsening of the other one. To evaluate the relation between the criteria values, the notion "price-of-fairness" was introduced. This contribution is focused on approaches to the two objective emergency medical service system design, when the system criterion is optimized subject to limited price-of-fairness.

articleTitle: Industry 4.0 and labour law - Does law 4.0 exist?
abstract: The fourth industrial revolution has brought numerous innovations which have significant effects on workplaces, and so, on the changes in working conditions and the labour market itself. The fourth industrial revolution means the new era of mechanization and automation, which is also strengthened by the digitalization of work. Because of this, several questions emerge that should be solved and regulated by the tools of the law. This is a multifaceted problem. Law as a universal system is only partly affected by the phenomenon. As a result, the regulation process itself is not too fast. The other question is to what extent soft law solutions can play a role. The legislator is in this period now, when it defines white books, strategies, and other soft law tools. Should it take more drastic steps? Before answering these questions, it is essential to state that law is a following system. It always follows technical development, and usually not generates it. Moreover, the law is a linear system, while the technical and digital development of nowadays is cyclic and periodical. What is considered a world-saving technical innovation on one day, tortures to be a deadline on the other? Law and rather the legislators need to wait for being able to follow the mainstream of development. These periods are often ex-lex periods. The legislator tries to create a regulation based on the experience gained in the meantime. But is the legislator prepared? Can it prepare for constituting law which can manage the life situations created by Industry 4.0? Because of the extent of limits, the complete legal context cannot be examined in this study. And it is not even the goal. However, we would like to present the areas most affected by the changes. Searching for the answer to the questions above, primarily labour law and the related social law will be examined, as the direct effect of the fourth industrial revolution can be observed in the workplace. A typical question always emerging in connection with this topic should also be answered: "Will many people lose their jobs because of automation and robotization?" If this is true, then are the current legal tools enough to manage the situation? Is fourth-generation law necessary for solving emerging situations? And the most important question: is the legislator able to constitute such a law if necessary?

articleTitle: Benchmark example for the Heuristically accelerated FRIQ-learning
abstract: Heuristically accelerated FRIQ-learning (HFRIQ-learning) is a Fuzzy Rule-Interpolation based Q-learning method which is able to embed external expert knowledge into the learning system. It usually speeds up the learning process, but in case if the expert knowledge describes an incorrect solution, it could also have a negative effect on the learning performance. In HFRIQ-learning, the Q-function knowledge representation is a state-action-value sparse (fuzzy rule interpolated) rule-base. The expert knowledge usually expressed by production (state-action) rules. This paper briefly introduces the way how the HFRIQ-learning optimises the Q-function rule-base and how it locates and corrects the incorrect expert rules. The paper also demonstrates the effect of the expert knowledge quality on the HFRIQ-learning performance on a popular reinforcement learning benchmark example.

articleTitle: Model-based Prototyping of a Controller for MR Actuators
abstract: Magnetorheological (MR) actuators are semi-active devices that leverage the smart properties of the MR fluids whose rheology can be controlled by an external magnetic field. Within the presence of an external magnetic field, the magnetic domains of the MR fluid align with the external field, which results in the yield stress induced in the fluid, thus undergoing a transition from a fluid to a semi-solid. Thus, the control challenge for MR actuators is in controlling the rheology of the material by magnetic flux. Typically the control system is based on the coil’s current feedback. However, this approach based purely on the current control is not optimal since it is the magnetic stimuli that directly controls the material’s yield stress and not the current. Thus, this work investigates the capability of a flux controller in handling the non-linearities of the actuator, including magnetic hysteresis. A model of an MR actuator that incorporates the magnetic hysteresis and the control coil dynamics is developed. The flux controller is tuned to handle the addition of the hysteresis effect. The obtained results show that the chosen control topology is very effective for the considered flux commands inputs.

articleTitle: The advantage of smart manufacturing systems using cloud and RAMI 4.0
abstract: The article presents an empirical analysis of the benefits of cloud manufacturing, the need to consider the Reference Architecture Model Industry 4.0 (RAMI 4.0), and, last but not least, IoT applications. Using high-performance and complex platforms, it is possible to modernize automation, tracking, and control systems, with the condition of completing optimization systems to increase performance. The article attempts a theoretical approach to cloud systems that has implications in production systems. RAMI offers an analysis of the entire production system, a system that can be analyzed, interpreted and ensures optimal functioning through intervention. Cloud manufacturing provides an overview of the entire production system with all resources used, but also an overview of actions to optimize the production system. In order to be able to draw the most relevant conclusions in real-time, we simulated such a system using Petri nets. Petri nets are chosen because they are easier to interpret, provide real-time information, and are relatively easy to modify the system proposed for simulation, so that decisions can be made as quickly as possible without disrupting the production system. This article focuses more on the relationship between cloud manufacturing and RAMI 4.0. The advantages of this approach are computational speed and storage capacity without investing in additional configurations, user data synchronization, and data processing. The downside is that it wants to find a solution for data security, which leads to mistrust among users. The case study is applied to a module of the production system because the system is complex and can provide easy-to-interpret results for the decision-making unit.

articleTitle: Inspection results map module for a metrological calibration and verification system to support the Smart City Vision
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is the natural response to the need of collecting remote data, to monitor and to remote control hardware devices, given the advancements in the telecommunication field. Started in 1980’s as an application to remotely monitor the supply level of a vending machine placed in a university campus, coined as term by Kevin Aston in 1999, the IoT was used by more than 25% of businesses at 2019 level, and gained popularity as a remote tool for home appliances. A branch of IoT is represented by urban IoT systems, designed to support the smart city vision - Smart City, which seeks to exploit the most advanced communication technologies to support value-added services for city administration and citizens; up until the present, the main developments in this area was conducted toward smart traffic / parking management, and air quality monitoring.

articleTitle: Assessment of the possibilities of using statistical process control tools in metallurgical production
abstract: In accordance with the principles of sustainable development, effective recovery of raw materials from the recycling process and their reuse by returning them to the production cycle helps preserve nonrenewable raw material resources. There is an ongoing effort to constantly improve the technologies used, increase their efficiency, and minimize their negative impact on the environment. It is important for a production company to consistently monitor and control its processes. One of the tools that make this possible is the Statistical Process Control (SPC) tools. By implementing these tools in the production processes, an organization can assess the state of the process based on regulated parameters and eliminate the impact of random (external) influences through appropriate interventions. With a stable process, it is possible to ensure that the output of the process is as close as possible to the required (target) value with minimal deviations. This paper presents a research of the pyrometallurgical processing of raw materials with different copper content and an assessment of the possibility of active use of the SPC tools in the monitoring and controlling processes to increase their quality and efficiency is evaluated.

articleTitle: Opportunities and Major Risks of Implementing Cloud - computing and IOT in Public Healthcare
abstract: Digitalization in healthcare is evolving rapidly with endless opportunities. Digital health itself is described as an integration of information technology and electronic communications used for different kind of healthcare processes, tools or methods e.g. digital patient records, remote patient monitoring, booking option for a medical appointment through the internet, electronic ordering of medicine and it also means having digital accessibility and storage for medical images, laboratory results, and hospital final reports for anybody who has eligibility and needs of these. They became more and more widely known and used during the COVID19 pandemic. Digitalization stepped out through the hospital wall as well, so patients and medical staff are now able to access to the information and data they need through their smart devices from any location. These new things are using mainly a special network concept that appeared on the market around 2007 and it is called cloud computing. This technology is playing a leading and important role in digital transformation in health care also. This paper is intending to demonstrate this technology using in public health care, identify the main benefits and highlight the possible risks. To demonstrate the risk factors, I am using the Risk Assessment Matrix, also known as a Probability and Severity risk matrix to classify and identify them such as cyberattacks, any downtime on the cloud platform side, extra load in LAN, loosing network connection, difficulties regarding procurement and operation or lack of IT knowledge of the hospital staff. At the end of the paper, I also provide some ideas and solutions how to reduce the possible risks and to run a safe and successful operation in a hospital.

articleTitle: Microprocessor load measurement in an embedded system
abstract: Embedded systems often use FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) chips for their implementation. Soft processors are optimized for their implementation in such circuits. Embedded system processor load is crucial when real-time applications are implemented. Processor load can be analyzed in several ways. The application described in this paper demonstrates a possible method to analyze the processor behavior and a model was developed, which is able to classify processor load. The model was implemented in FPGA without any modification of the original embedded system. The results of the analysis mark the time periods when the processor is overloaded.

articleTitle: Research study of image classification algorithms based on Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: The beginning of the paper introduces the idea of neural networks by presenting the neuron models and artificial neural networks. Next, the flow of operations used in the development of convolutional neural networks is presented, as well as an overview of popular architectures used in model development. After introducing the theoretical issues, a project using the EfficientNet architecture to recognize medical images taken by MRI is presented. The project describes: the selection and parameters of the MRI image database representing different types of brain tumors, the process of implementation and appropriate modification of the EfficientNet architecture used to classify images, the presentation of the results of learning the convolutional neural network and the images that highlight on the basis of which area the convolutional neural network classifies images.

articleTitle: The Use of Genetic Algorithm for PID Controller Auto-Tuning in ARM CORTEX M4 Platform
abstract: It is known that the Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) controller is still the most used control device in the industry, due to its efficiency, ease of implementation and wide applicability. However, the controller tuning also presents some difficulties. Within this context, this work presents a practical implementation for PID controller auto-tuning using genetic algorithms embedded in the ARM Cortex microcontroller. The results showed efficient applicability for the controlled system.

articleTitle: Graphical Interface for Behavioral Studies on a Hexapod Robot
abstract: This paper presents the main elements in the development of a graphical interface for the behavioral studies on a hexapod robot. The Matlab environment and the facilities of its GUIDE editor were used. The interface is organized zonally and allows the simple modification of numerous constructive and functional parameters of the robot to evaluate its behavior. The interface also provides supervised control when entering the desired data to prevent errors or unrealistic situations. One of the final goals was to study relative to the essential classes of obstacles specific to walking robotics. Further developments of the interface also allowed coupling with a simplified physical model of the hexapod robot to allow evaluations between simulations and real physical behaviors.

articleTitle: Identify the objective parameters of direct communication between PLC and MS SQL server
abstract: When building digital twins of existing technical solutions, we need a large amount of data on the parameters of their operation under various conditions. The source of data on the values of process variables at the lowest level is control devices - most often PLCs. There are many ways to acquire the qualities of process variables available from the PLC level. Increasingly, OPC UA is replacing the OPC model, and the OPC UA server is increasingly a functionality of the PLC CPU. The Industrial Internet of Things IIoT is used in companies moving toward Factory 4.0. Data from controllers can be acquired using high-level languages such as C++, C# or Python. Libraries often made available under an open-source license are used for this. For example, you can find commercial libraries for communication between PLCs of selected manufacturers and MySQL servers. Siemens provides a library for communication between S7-1200/1500 controllers and MS SQL server. The author has yet to find an exhaustive analysis of such a solution. In the literature, there need to be more studies of experiments describing the performance of query generation and execution and the impact of the library on PLC performance. The article presents the results of an experimental study of this issue.

articleTitle: Optimal Selection of Pharma Stock Portfolios using DEPSO
abstract: In this study, the objective function value and optimal allocation of seven different stocks of actual pharmaceutical companies are determined using a novel search technique that combines DE and PSO. The research assesses the effectiveness of the current nonlinear solver in LibreOffice Calc and demonstrates how they may be quickly applied in pharmaceutical portfolio selection to move beyond the Mean-Variance Optimization/Quadratic Programming paradigm. An experimental model was solved based on one-year real historical data to demonstrate the effectiveness of the nonlinear solver. Evaluation findings show that the above approach is effective and useful for solving the portfolio selection model.

articleTitle: Characterization and Modeling of a Microwave Reactor for the Open-Loop Control of its Impedance
abstract: In the context of controlling a microwave chemical reactor, this article presents an approach to address the reflection of electromagnetic waves caused by impedance mismatch. Microwave chemistry is a technique that has a lot of advantages compared to conventional methods, but its major drawback is the reflection of EM waves by the microwave cavity. One of the ways to overcome this problem is to use a triple stub tuner and adjust it according to the impedance of the reaction medium. In this manuscript, a numerical model that characterizes the system as well as simulation results of the model are shown, in addition to experimental results to validate the proposed model. De-embedding and the cascade methods have been adopted in this work which show promising results to address the energy transfer problem.

articleTitle: Closed Circuit Root Locus Calculation Based on A Given Open Circuit Transfer Function in A MATLAB Environment
abstract: For the adjustment of control circuits, it is crucial to verify their stability and the extent of changes in some parameters of the controller, such as proportional gain. The calculation procedure uses an algorithm to determine the roots of a polynomial in the transfer function's denominator, which is part of Matlab. An example will demonstrate the use of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Using the EMG Signal to Control a Wheelchair
abstract: Among the most important human needs is the desire to live as comfortably and independently as possible. Nothing bothers the patient so much as the infirmity of his own body, often resulting in a high dependence on the care of others, even during simple everyday activities. The ability to move and manipulate objects in the human environment is the basis of human functioning. At the same time, such simple activities are a huge problem for many people, and sometimes even an unattainable barrier to a better life. The reasons for this situation vary, ranging from genetic defects, through various types of diseases, to injuries and accidents, which in drastic cases may even result in amputations of parts of the human body. The article presents aspects related to the measurement of the signal of electrical activity of skeletal muscles (EMG) and the simulation results of the recorded signal use to control the device operation, e.g. in the form of a wheelchair, which is an aid for the patient in moving around.

articleTitle: Prototype of Software-Defined Self-Calibrating Temperature Compensated Oscillator
abstract: Distributed systems employ network time and frequency synchronization, typically IEEE 1588 PTP or its derivatives, to achieve a common, synchronized time and frequency on all nodes. Time and frequency synchronization is required as the oscillators of nodes produce non-ideal clock signals to drive the operation of the individual nodes, i.e., their frequencies deviate from the nominal one by an oscillator-specific static offset and a continuously changing drift. Network time and frequency synchronization operate when nodes can successfully communicate with the primary (reference) clock. During this process, they measure their actual deviations from the primary clock and compensate for that by applying a node-specific method. However, when communication fails with the primary clock, the node goes into the so-called holdover mode, and it starts to deviate from the primary clock due to drift. The main source of drift is temperature variations for most of the applications. Temperature Compensated Oscillators (TCXO) and Oven Controlled Oscillators (OCXO) are developed to keep oscillator temperature-related frequency deviations low, however, these devices are substantially more expensive than standard oscillators, they are bigger, and they use more power also, so they are not an option in a large number of applications. However, it is possible to augment the oscillator with low-cost temperature sensors (e.g. thermistor), and in normal synchronized operation collect information about the frequency-temperature relationship of the oscillator and build a model of it, then apply this model in holdover mode to reduce temperature related drift. In essence, we construct a low-cost, self-calibrating Software-Defined Temperature Compensated Oscillator (SD-TCXO) with this approach. The paper introduces a hardware and software prototype for the SD-TCXO, and initial performance data about its evaluation.

articleTitle: Second-Order Statistical Techniques for Enhancing Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio
abstract: This study explores the use of cognitive radio as a solution to the problem of radio spectrum scarcity and ineffectiveness. The focus is on spectrum sensing, a critical aspect of cognitive radio with various algorithms. The research examines a spectrum sensing algorithm based on the cyclic prefix correlation coefficient in OFDM signals(Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing). The detection threshold is determined using a constant false alarm rate and a method for minimizing the average total error probability. Additionally, a formula for normalized spectrum utilization for primary and secondary users is presented. The results of the simulation show improved performance of the detector through the use of an adaptive threshold, resulting in a 6 dB increase in the probability of detection at 0.6 compared to a fixed threshold. The normalized spectrum utilization improved by approximately 5% at SNR = -12 dB for a spectrum occupancy of 0.5 and by 25% at SNR = -20dB for a spectrum occupancy of 0.7.

articleTitle: Modelling and Optimization of Commuter Flows as Queuing System Considering Customer and Environmental Costs: a Case Study
abstract: Passenger flows in transportation systems need to be controlled in such a way that costs are minimized. To be able to do it, discrete event systems can be used for the first model and then optimize in transportation systems. Queuing systems in particular are often the means of choice to model transportation systems in order to minimize costs. In the past, the focus has been on minimizing customer or supplier costs. In this paper, the theory of queuing systems is applied to model commuter flows between a fixed origin and destination, considering the L-BFGS-B optimization algorithm. It is known that limited-memory BFGS (L-BFGS or LM-BFGS) is an optimization algorithm in the family of quasi-Newton methods and that the L-BFGS-B algorithm extends L-BFGS to handle simple box constraints variables. Due to climate change, environmental factors are increasingly important, which is why not only customer costs but also environmental costs are considered in the novel model, presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Modelling hysteresis with neural network
abstract: An example of a system with hysteresis is an actuator made of SMA. In the paper, the LSTM neural network was used to model the actuator. The focus was pointed to its hysteretic part. Neural network structure and learning method are briefly presented. Data used for training was obtained from the Preisach hysteresis model. This model was used to generate the datasets used for training and testing. Thanks to this approach, we can generate data quickly and in a fully controllable way. Thanks to this, experiments can be thoroughly planned and fully repeatable. The advantage and disadvantage at the same time is the lack of disturbances. The main goal of the paper was to model hysteresis on an example of an SMA actuator, but in fact, it was interesting if a neural network could describe hysteresis loop because literature research shows that usually neural networks are used to model hysteresis with a hysteretic element in combination modelled in another way.

articleTitle: Current State and Development Context for a Product Model Based on Digitization and Document Management at Enterprise Level
abstract: This paper presents the current state of the market, the modern technologies used, and what the new project aims to bring in addition to current products. The need for the project proposal is generated by the new Industry 4.0 trend in the field of industrial and business applications, based on the exchange of data in and between manufacturing processes. This includes Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), Cloud Computing, distributed computing, applications, information access and storage.

articleTitle: Experimental design with a purpose to improve industrial processes and waste water treatment
abstract: The current time, when the competition in the market is very strict, requires not only the prescribed quality of the products sold but also high production efficiency. Experimental design is a useful tool for improving the results of industrial processes and for improving the processes themselves. The publication deals description of the design of experiments in industrial processes with a purpose to improve industrial processes and regard to the limited resources of the experiment.

articleTitle: Information management, from Client applications, through TCP / IP Communication on interrupts, in a Multiclient-Server application
abstract: This paper presents the management of several intelligent devices, connected in an Ethernet (TCP/IP) communication network with operation based on interruptions. The implementation of the same sampling period as a whole, for the entire distributed application of the Multiclient-Server type, is evaluated. In this work, an approach is presented, in an attempt to adopt as much as possible of the principles of a real-time distributed application, in the context of the concept of Digital Enterprise.

articleTitle: Acoustic Analysis of a Performance Hall Using Virtual Techniques
abstract: It is known that the acoustics of a performance hall are important for the performance of artistic events. The paper presents a methodology for determining and analysing the acoustic parameters for a performance hall under construction. First, the room was three-dimensionally scanned to obtain a geometric model in a virtual environment. The initial "points cloud" was processed using specific reverse engineering techniques and methods. Thus, irregularities of a geometric nature, such as non-conforming surfaces, spikes and self-intersections, were eliminated. Also, the "points cloud" was transformed into elementary triangular surfaces. These were unified and transformed into larger continuous surfaces. Then, this surface-based geometry was transformed into virtual solids. This geometry was compared with the initial plan of the performance hall. Finally, the geometric model was imported into a finite element analysis software. In this program, the materials were attached to the solid elements of the model, then the constraints and acoustic sources were defined. The model was divided into finite elements and the simulation was run. Results maps were obtained and further analysed and compared. Based on these results, significant conclusions were drawn.

articleTitle: Distributed supervision of an edge micro datacenter
abstract: This paper presents novel hierarchical management architecture of heterogeneous edge data center. The management architecture was implemented in BRAINE (Big data pRocessing and Artificial Intelligence at the Network Edge) project. One of the key objectives of this project was to develop an energy efficient heterogeneous 3U Edge Micro Data Center (EMDC) including all PCBs, thermal subsystem and mechanics. The BRAINE’s Edge framework is designed to be flexible and support many types of data processing and storage cards. Because of this flexibility and the wide range of heterogeneous cards a sophisticated and hierarchical board/card management functionality is needed. The hierarchical system management consists of a central board management node (BMC: Board Management Controller), and a distributed low-level board management hardware present on all the nodes or cards (BMMC: Board Management MicroController). The goal of this paper is to describe the functionalities and present implementation details of this multi-fold low level interconnection and the services being provided.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of Tandem Substring Search Methods
abstract: Strings and lists play a fundamental role in data structures. Considering string operations, one of the key functions is the search for matching parts within a given host string. The location of repeating substring pattern is a special type of general substring search. This task is of outstanding importance, among other in biology (examining genes problem) or in process modeling (searching for cycles). This article presents a specific alternative method for tandem substring search which unlike the traditional, direct pattern search methods presents, is based on the application of neural networks. The performed comparative analyzes carried out show that a neural network-based methods is a good alternative, especially in the case of approximate searches.

articleTitle: Monitoring of MPPT regulation during temperature transient phenomenon in off-grid solar system
abstract: During temperature transient phenomenon the electrical parameters of solar cell change rapidly. Increasing temperature affect decreasing voltage, which requires the rapid intervention of the control circuit to find a new maximum power point. The investigated solar panel works under laboratory conditions in an off-grid system. Battery pack and DC load have been also connected to the MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) to simulate the normal operation.

articleTitle: Comparation of Rotational Deep Learning based Methods
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) imagery-based object detection has become more and more widespread, especially in fields like agriculture, city planning, construction oversight or even military reconnaissance. This research focused on a review of the state-of-the-art object detection algorithms which use oriented bounding boxes. The images were collected using DJI Tello and Zll SG906 Pro 2. The images were annotated using Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT). The different detectors were trained using MMDetection and MMRotate modules from MMLab framework. The advantages and disadvantages of different deep neural network approaches are aimed to be compared: Rotated Faster R-CNN (two-stage anchor based detector), Single Shot Alignment Network (S<sup>2</sup>ANet) (one-stage anchor detector) and FCOSR (one-stage anchor-free detector). On neural network models two series of measurements were performed. In the first version, all the image samples were trained during the epochs. In the second version the images were grouped in tasks, and in each epoch a new tasks were load to train. Based on the measurement results, it can be concluded that better results were achieved with the Rotated Faster R-CNN model and the S<sup>2</sup>ANet model, the FCOSR performance lagged behind the previous models.

articleTitle: LQR and Pole Placement Controllers with Integral Action Design Technique and Performance Analysis for Control of Temperature Field in Continuous Casting Process
abstract: This paper presents the design of Linear Quadratic Regulator and Pole Placement controllers with integral action using MATLAB and Simulink for controlling the temperature field in the secondary cooling zone of a continuous casting process. The secondary cooling zone in continuous casting represents a distributed parameter system. During steel production, the type of steel produced changes continuously, necessitating a control system that can respond quickly and flexibly. We compared the performance of the Linear Quadratic Regulator and Pole Placement control techniques for the temperature field in the secondary cooling zone by analyzing the system’s response. The simulation results demonstrate that the Linear Quadratic Regulator technique outperforms the Pole Placement technique for the specified system.

articleTitle: Uninterruptible induction motor drive in combination with an off-grid solar inverter
abstract: The study presents an uninterruptible induction motor drive, in combination with an off-grid solar inverter. The article highlights the advantages of combining the two systems and mention the necessary system elements. It also presents the total harmonic distortion and operating parameters for different system topologies. The transients of the combined network are also presented in the form of simulations. The results were obtained based on simulations in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Using Deep Reinforcement Learning to Solve a Navigation Problem for a Swarm Robotics System
abstract: Five mobile robots in a swarm are trained in this paper using the deep reinforcement learning method to solve a navigation problem with two targets without prior knowledge of the environment. The Proximal Policy Optimization method trains E-puck mobile robots to avoid obstacles while completing tasks in the shortest distance for each robot. A Webots simulator is used to model the environment in three-dimension space. The suggested algorithm works with continuous states derived from eight infrared sensors and continuous action spaces that reflect the velocities of two motors for each robot in the swarm. Then the robot's behavior will be examined in light of two categories of rewards: Spares and Shaping rewards. If the environment's complexity is not decreased, proximal policy optimization with spare rewards will not be able to train every robot in the system how to accomplish its goal. Compared to the spare rewards technique, shaping rewards aid the robot in gaining experience from prior knowledge during the training process. This speeds up learning and aids navigation in more complex environments.

articleTitle: The Development of an Application to Analyse GigE Vision Packets
abstract: The focus of a previous research at the University of Miskolc was the determination of the speed of high-speed rotating parts. A non-contact measurement procedure using a line scan camera was developed. During the examination of the camera using the Gigabit Ethernet (GigE) Vision standard interface, it was suggested that image data processing can be improved by pre-processing the Ethernet packets. Verification of this proposition requires the examination of GigE Vision packets, which is the purpose of the application presented in this article.

articleTitle: The planning of neurosurgical operations: methods and criteria for determining the safest tool trajectory from the skull surface to the tumour
abstract: Methods of surgical plan determination are the topic of this paper. Neurosurgical operations are especially dangerous because of the risk of damage important areas in the brain. Results of such damage can be patient's death or loss of health. The finding of the safest tool trajectory from skull surface to tumour is the goal of operation plan. This trajectory should allow access to tumour located in deep parts of the brain and avoid zones which damage is especially dangerous. Security criteria used to determine optimal trajectory of surgical tool tip are presented an compared in this paper. Stages of plan development and mathematical formulas are described. Simulation tests of proposed methods were performed on exemplary models and results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: The evaluation of the steelmaking process using statistical indicators and regression models
abstract: The steelmaking process using Basic Oxygen Furnace (BOF) is one of the essential processes within the metallurgical technological chain. This process's most important quality output parameters are the steel's chemical composition and the steel's temperature, which are essential in terms of further processing of the steel. These parameters are affected by input parameters of the process such as, e.g., temperature, weight and the composition of pig iron, weight and the composition of steel scrap, amount of blown oxygen, etc. The statistical evaluation methods of various processes belong amongst basic qualitative methods that enable us to analyze and compare data on various quantitative parameters. Moreover, they make it possible to design appropriate interventions to improve these processes. The paper describes using statistical indicators for analyzing of BOF process and proposes of statical regression model for the temperature of the melt.

articleTitle: Autonomous robot control using hardware accelerated implementation of fuzzy interpolation
abstract: The FIVE (Fuzzy Interpolation in Vague Environment) is a possible method for behavior based control. Mobile robots can be also controlled by a behavior based controller. In addition to software implementations, FIVE also has a hardware implementation, which was implemented in FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) using Verilog hardware description language.The hardware implemented behavior control using the FIVE method was demonstrated on a line follower robot application, which is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimal sizing of battery storage for photovoltaic systems
abstract: In the future, photovoltaic systems with battery backup will be much more important. They reduce the load on the network, because electricity produced and not used during peak hours can be stored locally and thereby reduce the losses caused by its transmission over long distances. An optimally selected battery capacity can provide better performance for energy systems. Furthermore, batteries increase the self-consumption and autonomy of households and thus help to reduce energy costs. Currently, the economic situation is also a consideration for consumers when choosing photovoltaic system with battery bank. The goal is to minimize the life cycle costs of energy systems, which are initial investment costs and operating costs. This article focuses on finding the optimal size and operating conditions for a battery energy storage system used for solar photovoltaic systems, taking into account economic aspects to minimize the cost of the battery energy storage system.

articleTitle: Vehicle Control Modeling and Simulation for Small Electric Car Case
abstract: Lately, worldwide, there is an increasing interest in the development of electric vehicles that can also have intelligent capabilities so that they can then be transformed into autonomous vehicles. In this context, this paper presents an intuitive and reliable mathematical model that is the basis of the construction of a cruise control system dedicated to small electric vehicles both for outside and inside of industrial facilities in the context of sustainable development.

articleTitle: Temperature mapping in the storage area
abstract: The article deals with temperature mapping in the storage area, where it is necessary to maintain a stable temperature. A temperature change of a few degrees can affect product quality and safety. The measured temperatures were analyzed using descriptive statistics. The influence of the season on the temperature in the storage space was investigated. Quality management tools were used to investigate the problem of temperature changes. Brainstorming was used to search for possible ideas and causes of temperature changes in the controlled space. Then, the ideas were grouped into categories and recorded in an affinity diagram. Based on the findings, appropriate measures were proposed to maintain a stable temperature in the storage area. The appropriate measures can serve as general recommendations for temperature-controlled storage.

articleTitle: Verification of the Selected Vision System Reliability for Objects Detection Purposes
abstract: today, in more complex automated processes, the use of vision systems is considered necessary. Moreover, image recognition and detection have become an integral part of checking the shape properties of products or detecting defects in the material of end products and semi-finished products. This article, in the first part, points out the basic and advanced software options of the programming interface of the selected 2D vision system. The next part focuses on testing and verifying the reliability of image detection on the tested subject (bearing in the case) under static light conditions. Three independent modules were used in experiments, and combining them, a complete detection of the tested subject was built. The devices' interconnection responsible for detection results (OK/NOK) is also described in the article. Also, obtained results are represented as the optical visualization at the tested workplace.

articleTitle: A preliminary measurement verification of sound power level emitted by biomimetic drone propellers inspired by an owl’s feather
abstract: The research issue addressed in the project is to investigate methods of reducing acoustic emissions of unmanned aerial vehicle propellers. S.O.W.A (Silent Observer of the Wild Animals) is an arrangement that mimics the structure of an owl’s feathers. Rotor blades based on owl feathers have been constructed to suppress the noise produced during flight. Acoustic emissions, were measured with accordance to ISO 3741:2010. Sound power level of different design variants was discussed.

articleTitle: Detection of Handwriting Characteristics using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents an application based on image processing techniques that use deep neural networks in the field of psychology. The approach proposed in the paper automates the well-known methods of determining the main personality traits using graphological analysis (handwriting analysis). The study is based on three characteristics of handwriting: baseline, word slant and writing pressure. To achieve this goal, three VGG-16 Convolutional Neural Networks were trained using a database of handwriting samples. The results obtained are promising, with an accuracy between 78% and 92%. Also, the image processing speed (after training the network) is very high with values around 60 sec.

articleTitle: Suboptimal State Feedback H2 Control of Positive Linear Systems
abstract: In this paper, the state control problem is studied for a class of linear continuous-time positive systems with dynamics defined by the system matrix of a purely Metzler structure. By preserving the closed-loop system positivity and asymptotic stability, the auxiliary goal is to ensure combined compactness of the system performance within H<inf>2</inf> norm limit and Metzler parametric constraints. The LMI-based numerical method is presented to provide an optimal solution of this diagonal stabilization problems, where sufficient conditions for the existence of a non-negative gain of the control law are given in terms of a feasible set of linear matrix inequalities. The theory and the algorithm behavior are illustrated by a numerical example and detailed discussed to put in evidence the efficiency of the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Modeling temperature distribution using a mathematical method
abstract: During reflow soldering of the PCB (Printed Circuit Board), the soldering quality can be improved by knowing the temperature distribution. In practice, it is only possible to measure the temperature in a few places, which limits the setting of the appropriate thermal profile. The article models the temperature distribution using the inverse distance weighting method. The article shows the application of the method through a practical example. It shows a solution for checking the modeled values.

articleTitle: A Performance Evaluation of Two Blockchain Platforms for a Use Case
abstract: This paper describes the results of benchmarking two blockchain platforms’ performance. The authors conducted a performance assessment of various actions including adding, editing, deleting, and selecting the data from a blockchain. The blockchain platforms were run locally, in Ganache for Ethereum and IBM Blockchain Platform for Hyperledger Fabric. Additionally, code optimizations at the smart-contract level resulted in higher test speeds for both cases. The experimental case consisted in storing students’ diploma identification numbers, with the practical aim of preventing document forgeries.

articleTitle: Execution of Resource Intensive Tasks on a Heterogeneous SoC for Low-Latency Embedded Compute
abstract: Execution of resource-intensive tasks, such as artificial intelligence (AI), big-data algorithms, video processing, etc. is a common requirement in distributed embedded systems today. The typical solution is to execute such algorithms on some cloud computing service, as embedded systems do not have the computing resources for such tasks. However, this approach is not viable in Real-Time Cyber-Physical Systems (RT-CPS) due to the high-latency, non-real-time nature of cloud computing. The latency requirements can be only satisfied with an edge compute solution in the form of an edge data center or by a heterogeneous System on Chip (SoC) based implementation, which has the required high-performance computing resources on the chip. In the paper, we investigate the viability of the heterogeneous SoC compute approach on the Texas Instruments AM5729 SoC, which was specifically designed for such applications. The paper introduces the hardware capabilities of the SoC, the software development, and the run-time (Linux-based) environment, and presents the results of a detailed performance evaluation on relevant computing tasks.

articleTitle: Industrial application of hydrophone for condition monitoring of water pump
abstract: The hydrophone, also known as an underwater microphone, is placed in industrial tanks and converts sounds under water (or other liquids) into an electrical analogue signal. The bandwidth is typically the audible range, but they can also operate in the ultrasonic range, up to 1 MHz. The analogue signal from the hydrophone is digitized and the time-domain wave file is processed using Fast Fourier Transform to produce a power spectrogram, which is one of the key inputs for further data and signal processing. Artificial Intelligence Deep-Learning techniques help in the machine processing of large amounts of data and automatic classification. The Python package Librosa utilized for the features extraction of audio files. The waterfall spectrogram and RMS are basic tools in this analysis. The csv, numpy and pandas python packages are used to convert .wav files into .csv files on which data processing can be performed. The sklearn python package is used for preprocessing, and the keras and tensorflow python packages are used for model training and evaluation, and for building the neural networks. The trained model can be used to estimate which previous classified type a new sound sample may belong to. The precision of the model improved by raising the number of samples, but only to a certain limit, which must be determined appropriately.

articleTitle: Methods of Peripheral Synchronization in Real-Time Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Real-Time Cyber Physical Systems (RT-CPS) utilize network clock and frequency synchronization, typically IEEE 1588 PTP or its derivatives, to agree on a common time and frequency on all nodes. The knowledge of common time and frequency is required for in-phase sampling and actuation in the distributed system, and for timestamping based on the global clock. Modern network enabled microcontrollers (NeMCU) and embedded application processors support (EAP) IEEE 1588 in hardware; however, it means that only the physical hardware clock in the network interface controller (NIC) is synchronized, not the actual embedded peripherals, such as A/D and D/A converters, digital I/O ports, timers, PWM modules, or secondary communication interfaces. It is the task of the developer to devise a hardware and software solution for peripheral synchronization. In the paper we investigate how modern NeMCUs and EAPs support peripheral synchronization, and how one can construct synchronized peripherals utilizing the features of hardware and proper software. The findings of the paper are demonstrated by analyzing the performance of a synchronized sampling system (sound acquisition system) and an extended timestamp unit.

articleTitle: Design of a Mathematical Model of Pig Iron Cooling Between a Blast Furnace and an Oxygen Converter
abstract: Information about the temperature of pig iron between tapping from the blast furnace and pouring it into the oxygen converter is very important, especially from the point of view of process control as an input to the control system. However, pig iron is transported in a torpedo car and the possibilities of measuring the temperature of pig iron are limited and are connected only to some specific place and time. To know the temperature between these measurements, it is necessary to create a mathematical model as a tool that will allow establishing or indirectly measuring the temperature of the pig iron, specifically in the torpedo car. The article deals with the design of a mathematical model of pig iron cooling. Elementary models of partial processes such as heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation, as well as the accumulation of thermal energy, are described. The main mathematical model based on the heat balance of the process of cooling pig iron in the torpedo car is created from the elementary models. The mathematical model was implemented in the MATLAB environment. At the end of the article, examples of simulations are presented, and the possibilities of using the mathematical model are described.

articleTitle: How to DIY a wireless sensor node? - Case study on a node development
abstract: Within the increasing of technology development, measurements have become an important pillar in any system, where the basic point in this field is to deal with sensors, networks, or sensor networks. In our daily life, we are always surrounded by plenty of sensors in the aim to collect some data about the environment or forecasting to prevent some situations. This paper introduces a basic methodology of the development of a sensor node which collects temperature and humidity values and sends them to the cloud, where the aim from this work is to build a low-cost measurement system, which can be used to monitor houses or offices, and can help us to behave more environmentally friendly. With examining the collected data, we can make decisions to save energy.

articleTitle: Automatic Question Generation based on Sentence Structure Analysis
abstract: Automated question generation is a key problem in computational linguistics and knowledge engineering. There are different approaches and methodologies like template-based, syntax-based, or machine learning approaches. The paper investigates the efficiency and analysis of the role of the embedding module in sentence parsing. Embedding language models are important modules and the performed tests show that embeddings can provide a high accuracy in semantic-level similarity methods.

articleTitle: Conceptual Design and Control of a Robotic System for Welding
abstract: The use of Hierarchical Systems (HS) method in design and control of a robotic system for welding (RSW) is suggested in the paper. Created conceptual model of the robotic system under consideration integrates connected systemic descriptions of the RSW mechatronic subsystems – IT, electronic, mechanic – which are given in the common HS theoretical basis. RSW structure and the motion planning task, RSW dynamic presentation in its environment, RSW control unit, and RSW learning by demonstration processes are also given in this basis. The examples of the RSW control processes, robot teaching and welding process simulation using Mimicking Kit and RobWork program system respectively are also described in the work.

articleTitle: Transportation Systems for Intelligent Cities
abstract: The automation level of systems within smart city structures can be increased by implementing the new machine-to-machine (M2M) communication model. Also, transportation systems in modern society pose serious challenges. This type of implementation provides seamless integration of all the physical and virtual objects that are part of the smart city infrastructure. In vehicle technologies and their applications in various areas such as traffic management and information are being developed by automobile manufacturers. By integrating vehicles, technologies, sensing devices, and surveillance cameras, their sensing and communication capabilities can be leveraged to achieve intelligent transportation systems (ITS). leading to new challenges. Data latency and throughput requirements of certain applications within the smart city framework need to be addressed. The main goal of the suggested model is to improve the M2M nodes by creating an integrated system of electronic devices, communications, and sensors. They will be the link between smart cities and vehicles in the beginning. By integration of these components into the infrastructure of cities, it is likely that this technology will be applied to all manners of transportation in the future.

articleTitle: Requirements Analysis for a System for Certifying Online Content
abstract: This paper investigates the requirements for a system capable to authenticate (or certify) the content that is available online. Based on an analysis of the approaches used to fight against fake news and fake online content, our proposal is based on digital signatures, and integrates several key components to fulfill the determined functional requirements. This implies that both the origin of the text (the source) and the textual online content, can be trusted by anyone that is able to verify the applied electronic signature.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance in Twin Screw Air Compressors: a Case Study
abstract: The present paper proposes a predictive maintenance application to twin screw air compressors. An experimental setup was designed to acquire compressor operation data under different operating conditions. To detect the operating parameters of the compressor, the data acquisition system was realized exploiting Industry 4.0 concepts. An in-depth data analysis phase represented the initial point for the application and comparison of supervised machine learning techniques. The designed tool allows four operating conditions to be classified concerning the state of degradation of the oil used by the compressor, of the filters, of the separator, and of the power circuit. The results obtained from the experimental tests allowed to conclude that innovative techniques based on supervised machine learning can be applied to twin screw compressors, which are widely used in the industry, being able to perform predictive maintenance policies replacing the currently adopted periodic and corrective maintenance policies. The results obtained showed good values in terms of accuracy of the adopted models.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control of a 3-DOF Helicopter with State Dependent Regional Pole Placement
abstract: Sliding Mode Control methodologies are widely used to control uncertain and/or disturbed dynamical systems. The Sliding Mode Controller is designed so as the trajectories of the dynamical system are forced to stay on a stable hyper-surface which is pre-designed to shape the time response. This paper proposes a novel method confining the parameters (slopes) of the sliding surface while keeping the closed-loop system poles of the reduced order system without the control input expressing the null space dynamics in a desired region for a class of nonlinear systems. The traditional pole-placement approach attempts to locate the poles of the closed-loop system exactly at the desired locations. However, this approach provides a strict requirement for a nonlinear system since a nonlinear system usually shows different characteristics, mainly due to the uncertainties and state-dependent parameters. The proposed method eliminates this restriction by enabling the closed-loop system poles to stay inside a desired disk rather than force them to stay at some specific locations. The effectiveness of the proposed method and the effect of different disk parameters on the system responses are experimentally tested on the 3-DOF Helicopter test setup using three different disk parameters.

articleTitle: Case Study: Optimization of PI Controller Gains with Anti-Windup Applied on a Level System
abstract: It is known that Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers and their variations are widely used to control industrial processes, both in single-variable or in multivariable systems, which leads to its use in about 95% of industrial plants. In this context, this work presents the study of Proportional-Integral (PI) controller optimization gains with the anti-windup technique, applied to a level system from PD3 SMAR didactic plant, through Bee Swarm Optimization (BSO). For this, initially, the system open-loop response was obtained, under the application of first-order identification methods. Next, the PI controller was tuned using the BSO optimization algorithm, being compared with the Haalman classical tuning method, only for comparative analysis. For the results, of both controllers, a 40% Set-Point (SP) was performed using the Integral of the Squared Error (ISE) and Integral of the Quadratic Error multiplied by time (ITSE) performance indices for the control loop assessments. It was possible to observe that the PI controller tuned by the BSO algorithm obtained better performance. Therefore, it is worth highlighting how beneficial the optimization algorithm was compared to classical control techniques.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of a Low-bypass Turbofan with Coolant Injection into its Compressor
abstract: The author has studied an aircraft engine turbofan-type with low bypass ratio and two spools, fitted with a system for temporarily thrust augmentation (based on coolant injection method) subject to automatic control. Starting from turbofan’s non-linear motion equations, on which the gas-dynamic and thermodynamic influence of the coolant injection in front of the low-pressure compressor was highlighted, the mathematical model was established.
