New form of the model was issued, by using the finite differences method to bring it to a linear form; after convenient equations’ processing, they were brought to a dimensionless form; the Laplace transformation was applied, obtaining an accessible model form for further studies and a suggestive block diagram with transfer functions. Based on it, a quality study of the turbofan with thrust augmentation was carried out, considering some possible specific architectures, regarding step responses of dimensionless output parameters (spools’ speed and combustion chamber’s temperature), which provided some important conclusions about turbofan’s operation, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of using this kind of thrust augmentation method.

articleTitle: Cluster functionality validation by automated optical inspection
abstract: This paper proposes a Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) based solution for automated optical inspection and analysis of instrument clusters (IC) functionality. The work context resides in a research project thematic issued by the quality validation department within the local branch of one of the most important worldwide automotive manufacturers. The purpose of the automated optical inspection setup is to validate the correct functionality of the vehicle cluster during CAN communication, in different test scenarios. Following specific commands, the status of warning lights, telltales, custom pictograms, or text messages, is analyzed. Pattern matching by NCC is integrated in an NI LabVIEW application, which makes use of an industrial Basler camera and is supported by the NI Vision Development Module. The proposed application includes a custom collection of automated image analysis and processing methods, which help the core NCC approach. Supported by experimental results, an evaluation of the resulting NCC quality and usage feasibility, when applied to different visual elements present on a vehicle cluster, is presented. Once finalized, the proposed test system will be deployed for evaluation of IC functionality inside a climatic chamber. A report on different integration strategies applied with the purpose of maximizing IC optical test coverage and reducing test design effort and costs, is discussed.

articleTitle: From Toddlers to Experts - The Education of Robotics
abstract: Nowadays, and with the increasing demand to use the digital technologies and IT systems in our daily life and in industrial sectors, robotics has become an essential field that should deal with it, where we are surrounded by different kinds of robots, counting the basic ones as blender robot, cooker robot, cleaner robot, etc. The massive use of these systems can direct us to start thinking to deal with this field and bring it to the education in school, in order to raise a toddler to be an expert, the toddler can be in different ages with different capabilities, this paper presents a methodology related to robotics education, and how the robotics can be integrated into our thinking to understand the field well and upgraded it in the near future, by giving suggestions and solutions to create this direction into schools to develop the cognitive of the children regarding this concept.

articleTitle: A Customize Battery Management Approach for Satellite
abstract: A low-cost and reliable battery management unit for a student satellite was designed under the Pakistan National Student Satellite Program. Lithium-ion batteries were chosen as the secondary storage, and safety measures were incorporated to monitor, balance, and safeguard the cells. The main challenge was accurately measuring the voltage of individual cells, which was addressed using a resistive-divider network. Fast multiplexers and de-multiplexers were used to overcome the problem of insufficient I/O pins on the microcontroller. The design’s only limitation is the dissipation of heat due to dissipative resistors, but it is an optimal solution due to its cost-effectiveness and simplicity. This unique solution meets specific requirements, but more advanced and expensive designs are available.

articleTitle: rSOESGOPE Method Applied to Four-Tank System Modeling
abstract: It’s known that the design of identification signals plays a fundamental role in the estimation quality of dynamic systems models. Well-designed signals are able to excite the system’s dynamics to be later identified and represented in a model. This work presents the application of the rSOESGOPE (robust Sub-Optimal Excitation Signal Generation and Optimal Parameter Estimation) Method, which proposes the identification of robust parametric models from the use of multiple identification signals. In this perspective, the identification experiment is composed of optimized signals of the type Amplitude-modulated Pseudo Random Binary Signal (APRBS), designed by an approach composed of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and by the Interior-Point Method (IPM). To verify the effectiveness of the methodology, it was decided to study the classic problem of modeling the four-tank system, investigating the use of multiple optimized identification signals.

articleTitle: FPGA accelerated DeepSORT object tracking
abstract: Object detection and tracking is one of the most important vision algorithms in intelligent environments, applications based on it are the driving force behind the growing deployment of edge devices. As FPGAs can implement application specific hardware accelerators, they not only offer outstanding performance but also increased energy efficiency which is a very important factor in edge devices and the most recent FPGA families include processing elements which greatly increase the efficiency and performance of AI inference. In this paper we present a heterogeneous FPGA based implementation of the popular DeepSORT tracking algorithm.

articleTitle: Medical and technical requirements analysis for lower limb rehabilitation system
abstract: The last years have shown the need to use robotic systems for medical recovery activities. The paper presents this need and technical and medical requirements analysis for a lower limb rehabilitation system. A possible solution as a person to rebuild strength and coordination of a lower limb is rehabilitation robotics. The research is guided based on user-centered design. This paper presents the therapists’ answers to a questionnaire about the requirements of lower limb rehabilitation and a robotic rehabilitation system. Our development of a lower limb robotic rehabilitation device has to fulfill the needs and requirements of its users, both therapists and patients.

articleTitle: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus Prediction Model Based on Forecasting Algorithm
abstract: Forecasting, as an approach, performs an essential role in our life nowadays. Recently this technique has pervaded the healthcare field, where predictions can be simulated to prevent climacteric stages for the patient. This paper deals with T1D illness considered a chronic condition that constantly threatens the life of patients between the age of 4-14. The main problem of this illness is related to the lack of insulin in the blood. As the human body is designed as a black box, this research aims to understand the functioning of the body influencing the blood glucose value. The aim of this work is to build a system that predicts the change in blood glucose value in the future; the patients will be ready to schedule the different activities in their life and sufficiently handle their T1D. The system is based on machine learning models to forecast the future and maintain the glucose value in a safe range, avoiding critical cases. The data are from a 6-year-old child, where CNN, RNN and LSTM models are considered in this paper to make predictions; the obtained results show a good accuracy; meanwhile, other parameters could be added to have more promising results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency of the Gradual Refinement Approach
abstract: The gradual refinement approach has proved to be very efficient tool for finding a good approximation of the Pareto front consisting of various public service designs. The individual designs are represented by sets of p facility locations selected from m possible facility locations. Quality of a design is evaluated according two conflicting criteria, where one of them minimizes system disutility perceived by an average user and the second criterion minimizes disutility perceived by the most exposed users’ minority. The Pareto front consists of such designs that any other design is dominated by at least one of the Pareto front elements. The process of gradual refinement is based on step-by-step updating a current set of non-dominated system designs, when each step represents a neighborhood search procedure performed with one of the current set elements. Repeating of the process proved to be ineffective in comparison to the first application. This contribution is focused on enhancing efficiency of the gradual refinement by a special choice and treatment of the starting design after the first run of the original refinement process is performed.

articleTitle: Speed Control System for a Low-bypass Turbofan with Coolant Injection into its Compressor
abstract: In this paper a complex control system for an aircraft low-bypass turbofan engine is studied. The basic turbofan has two main governors – the fuel controller and, optional, the exhaust nozzle controller, but the coolant injection system has its own controller, which was added to engine’s basic control units. To describe the turbofan as controlled object one has considered as main outputs its spools’ rotational speeds (which are easily measurable parameters, proportional to turbofan’s thrust – its most important output). As secondary, but relevant output parameter, one has also considered the combustion chamber’s temperature. Appropriate architectures of main controllers (for fuel flow rate and for nozzle’s opening) were chosen and one has designed a suitable embedded control system, commanded by turbofan’s power lever position (engine’s single effective input). One has built up the embedded control system’s mathematical model (based on controllers’ models), as well as its block diagram. One has performed some Simulink-Matlab simulations, concerning system’s step responses, particularly for an existing turbofan and some conclusions about its behavior and its optional control architecture was revealed.

articleTitle: Cascade MIMO P-PID Controllers Applied in an Over-actuated Quadrotor Tilt-Rotor

authors.preferredName: José Luís Sousa de Magalhães Lima

abstract: To map the Virtual Control Actions (VCAs) into Real Control Actions (RCAs), over-actuated systems typically require nonlinear control allocation methods. On embedded robotic platforms, computational efforts are not always available. With this in mind, this work presents the design of a Quadrotor Tilt-Rotor (QTR) through a new concept of control allocation with uncoupled RCAs, where a nonlinear system is divided into partially dependent and linear subsystems with fast and robust convergence. The RCAs are divided into smaller and linearized sets and solved sequentially. Then, the cascade Multipe-Input-Multipe-Output (MIMO) Proportional (P)-Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) controllers tuning were presented with saturation constants and successive loop closure technique, where some open-field environment tests were conducted to validate the respective tuning. In the end, it showed to be reliable, robust, efficient, and applicable when VCAs are overlapped between the subsystems.

articleTitle: IoT module for a metrological calibration and verification system to support the Smart City vision. Implementation in urban transport
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is the natural response to the need of collecting remote data, to monitor and to remote control hardware devices, given the advancements in the telecommunication field. Started in 1980’s as an application to remotely monitor the supply level of a vending machine placed in a university campus, coined as term by Kevin Aston in 1999, the IoT was used by more than 25% of businesses at 2019 level, and gained popularity as a remote tool for home appliances. A branch of IoT is represented by urban IoT systems, designed to support the smart city vision - Smart City, which seeks to exploit the most advanced communication technologies to support value-added services for city administration and citizens; up until the present, the main developments in this area was conducted toward smart traffic / parking management, and air quality monitoring. In this context, the SmartTest research project aims to create a prototype equipment in form of an intelligent modular system for metrological calibration/verification for time and for distance parameters in urban transport, with robotic assistance and IoT functionalities, which will lead to the development of innovative products and services intended for metrological verifications in motor vehicle traffic – transport of goods but also of passengers.

articleTitle: Control and Supervisory Discrete Event Structures for Autonomous Vehicles in the Underwater Environment
abstract: The increasing complexity of the decision-making capability of underwater robotic systems raises important issues. Allowing an operator to define a vehicle mission in high-level language and translate it into a mission plan, and consequently develop appropriate tools to convert a mission plan into an operational mission program appears to be a significant goal in the underwater environment. In addition, equipping the operator with the ability to track the progress of the mission program as it is executed and the ability to modify it if necessary, improves mission performance in the underwater environment. For vehicles used in underwater missions to explore wide unknown areas, this is the main goal that a control architecture must enable. The present paper proposes a supervision system for autonomous underwater vehicles based on timed Petri nets. A detailed literature analysis is presented, assessing some important aspects of the considered topic. A novel modelization solution is proposed, based on suitable compositions of sequence, series and parallel structures.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Simulated Training Results based on Deep Learning and Battlefield Situation Awareness
abstract: Battlefield situation awareness is the basis of command decision in simulated battlefield combat training. The accuracy of battle commanders' judgements and decisions on the environment of the battlefield can be improved with the advancement of artificial intelligence technologies. In this paper, firstly, the calculation model of situation evolution speed is derived by simulating the self information of situation factors in battlefield training, and a case is analyzed with Markov chain; Then the cross entropy loss function of the deep learning model is derived from the evolution speed prediction model of the situation factors in the two-dimensional grid, which is equivalent to the evolution speed of the situation. Finally, the uncertainty of situation factors, the speed of situation evolution and the accuracy of training prediction are analyzed through the experimental results, and it is found that for the situation factors with randomness, the prediction accuracy has an extreme value.
